_README: Additional / curated sanctions lists loaded ONLY by scripts/sanctions-screen.mjs (not by the watcher's strict loader). A source may be remote (`url` + `parser`) or in-repo curated (`file`, parser 'curated'). Set `enabled:false` to keep a source configured but skipped. A remote source that fails or parses 0 names, or a curated list with no entries, degrades coverage (reported loudly) — never a silent all-clear.

sources.name: Argentina — RePET Entidades (terror-linked entities)
sources._note: RePET entidades — terror-linked ENTITIES sibling of the loaded personas.json (same /xml/ dir, keyless JSON). ENABLED 2026-08-05 on source-probe evidence (run 31030989375): the runner fetched real JSON (http 200, 156KB). The feed is the UN-consolidated-list schema in JSON (FIRST_NAME holds the entity name; ENTITY_ALIAS[].ALIAS_NAME the a.k.a. names) — hence parser 'unjson' (concatenates the ordered UN name parts and captures ALIAS_NAME), NOT the generic 'json' walker which read only FIRST_NAME and dropped the aliases.

sources.name: IDB — Dataset of Sanctioned Firms & Individuals (MDB cross-debarment)
sources._note: Inter-American Development Bank debarment dataset (2010 MDB Mutual-Enforcement cross-debarments: World Bank/ADB/AfDB/EBRD), ~1,500 firms/individuals; debarment (procurement-integrity) tier, not financial sanctions. STILL DISABLED — source-probe 2026-08-05 (run 31030989375): the old Socrata rows.csv endpoint now returns the IDB Open Data CKAN portal HTML page (generator 'ckan 2.11.4', doi:10.60966/7pfpgt0f), not a CSV — the dataset migrated off Socrata. The real download is a CKAN datastore/resource URL not yet identified; re-probe with the CKAN resource dump URL before enabling. parser 'socrata' left unimplemented (no proven CSV to map).

sources.name: Israel — NBCTF Terror Organization Designations (XLSX)
sources._note: Israel NBCTF ORGANISATIONS designation list — sibling of the loaded il-nbctf individuals file. ENABLED 2026-08-05 on source-probe evidence (run 31030989375): the runner fetched the real 323KB workbook (http 200, openxml). Header layout matches the individuals file (Hebrew captions row 0, English header row 1: 'Organization Name - Hebrew' + '… - aka' columns), which the XLSX reader's header-row scan handles; empty a.k.a. columns carry an all-dash '----' placeholder now skipped by the parser (never indexed as a name).

sources.name: Azerbaijan — FMS Domestic Sanctions List (XML)
sources._note: Azerbaijan State Security Service autonomous domestic designations. STILL DISABLED — source-probe 2026-08-05 (run 31030989375): http://hms.gov.az/en/olkedaxili-siyahi returns an HTML single-page app ('STATE SECURITY SERVICE / TARGETED FINANCIAL SANCTIONS'), not XML — the designations render client-side, no static XML at this URL. Enabling needs the JS app's underlying data endpoint (not discoverable from the sandbox); re-probe once that URL is found.

sources.name: Kyrgyzstan — FIU National Sanctions List (XML)
sources._note: Kyrgyzstan State Financial Intelligence Service national list (autonomous designations beyond UN). STILL DISABLED — source-probe 2026-08-05 (run 31030989375): https://fiu.gov.kg/sked/9?language=ru returns an HTML page (Yii app behind Cloudflare), not XML — the list is HTML-rendered, no static XML feed at this URL. Enabling needs either an HTML-table scraper or the app's data endpoint; re-probe once identified.

sources.name: UAE EOCN — Local Terrorist List
sources._note: EOCN publishes this only as PDF/Excel behind bot protection — no free machine-readable feed. Maintain the names in data/eocn-local-terrorist-list.json from the official EOCN download (https://www.uaeiec.gov.ae). While unpopulated it flags 'coverage incomplete', never a clean result.

sources.name: Internal — Firm Watchlist
sources._note: Firm-internal designations screened IN ADDITION to the official lists (checklist A4). `optional: true` — unlike official curated lists, EMPTY entries is a valid state ('no internal designations'): reported informationally, never degrades coverage. Maintain via the four-eyes SOP: docs/aims/eocn-list-update-sop.md §8.

sources.name: Canada — Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions (SEMA, XML)
sources._note: Best-effort generic-XML parse; if the structure changes it degrades visibly rather than silently.

sources.name: France — Registre national des gels (DGT)
sources._note: France DGT national freeze register (Registre national des gels). Re-enabled 2026-07-08 with the documented ApiPublic base path (the previous path 404'd); the generic JSON parser assembles Nom/Prenom + aliases. A failed fetch or 0-name parse degrades coverage loudly, never silently.

sources.name: New Zealand — Designated Terrorist Entities
sources._note: New Zealand designated terrorist entities: the Police publish the list only as XLSX/PDF documents with dated filenames — no stable machine-readable endpoint was found (probed 2026-07-08). Keep disabled until NZ publishes a stable feed, or maintain a curated file.

sources.name: Ukraine — NSDC State Register of Sanctions
sources._note: Ukraine NSDC State Register of Sanctions. 2026-08-05 survey verdict: api-drs.nsdc.gov.ua REQUIRES an API key granted only on written application (sanctions@rnbo.gov.ua) — rejected under the keyless doctrine, not merely unverified. Ukraine designations substantially overlap the EU/UK/US lists already screened daily; the ~15k register would be additive if Ukraine ever restores keyless access.

sources.name: Switzerland — SECO sanctions list (XML)
sources._note: Switzerland SECO consolidated sanctions list (Gesamtliste XML via the SESAM search service). Re-enabled 2026-07-08 with the dedicated parseSecoXml extractor (nested name-part/value blocks). SESAM generates the full-list XML server-side and needs well over the default 60s (both 2026-07-08 runs aborted at the flat timeout), hence the per-source 150s. A failed fetch or 0-name parse degrades coverage loudly.

sources.name: Switzerland — SECO Gesamtliste (curated fallback, in-repo)
sources._note: Activation switch the curated file's _README points at: paste the official designations into data/seco-curated-list.json (name/aliases rows), set its count/lastReviewed, then set enabled:true here. Kept disabled while entries is empty so an empty list can never read as screened coverage.

sources.name: Australia — DFAT Consolidated (OpenSanctions mirror)
sources._note: RETIRED 2026-08-05: the direct DFAT Improved Consolidated List proved on its first live run (11,068 names — richer than this mirror's 10,981), so the mirror is disabled. That removes the last OpenSanctions-hosted feed from this registry (their data licence is non-commercial; the official file is the license-clean path). Kept configured as a documented fallback should DFAT ever bot-block the runner.

sources.name: Australia — DFAT Consolidated List
sources._note: Australia DFAT 'Improved Consolidated List' (.xlsx, parseDfatXlsx reader). RE-ENABLED 2026-08-05 and PROVEN the same day: first live run loaded 11,068 names from the stable un-dated path — richer than the OpenSanctions mirror it replaces (10,981), which is now retired above. The registry's DFAT coverage is license-clean official data. A future bot-block fails loudly; the mirror entry stays as the documented fallback switch.

sources.name: Australia — DFAT Consolidated List (curated, in-repo)
sources._note: Activation switch the curated file's _README points at: paste the official designations into data/dfat-curated-list.json (name/aliases rows), set its count/lastReviewed, then set enabled:true here. Kept disabled while entries is empty so an empty list can never read as screened coverage.

sources.name: World Bank — Listing of Ineligible (Debarred) Firms & Individuals
sources._note: World Bank listing of ineligible (debarred) firms & individuals. DISABLED 2026-07-08: the apigwext gateway now answers HTTP 401 (verified on two live runs) — the endpoint requires an API key, and this system takes no per-source account/key dependencies. Debarment is procurement-eligibility data, not financial sanctions, so daily coverage is not weakened. Re-enable only if the Bank restores keyless access or publishes a static file.

sources.name: US Trade.gov — Consolidated Screening List (11 export-control + sanctions lists)
sources._note: Eleven US lists in one keyless bulk CSV — adds BIS Entity List / Denied Persons / Unverified and State Dept nonproliferation + statutorily-debarred parties the OFAC feeds do NOT carry (export-control axes directly relevant to precious-metals counterparties). US government work, public domain. parseCslCsv reads `name` + ';'-separated `alt_names`. Added 2026-08-05 from the worldwide-coverage survey; endpoint documented keyless — verify on the first live run (sandbox egress could not probe it).

sources.name: Sri Lanka — Competent Authority UNSCR 1373 National Designations (individuals)
sources._note: Sri Lanka national 1373 designations (XLSX). DISABLED — probe evidence 2026-08-05: connection fails from GitHub runners even with browser headers (DNS resolves, TLS/connection dies). Curated path, or periodic re-probe via source-probe.yml.

sources.name: Netherlands — National Sanctions List Terrorism (ODS)
sources._note: Dutch NATIONAL terrorism designations under the Sanctieregeling terrorisme (distinct from EU FSF). OpenDocument spreadsheet read by parseOdsList (same minimal ZIP reader as XLSX). Added 2026-08-05; verify on the first live run.

sources.name: Belgium — FOD Financiën consolidated financial sanctions (national additions)
sources._note: Belgian Treasury consolidated list — the ~180-entry NATIONAL terrorism additions (Royal Decree 28-12-2006) are the increment over the EU FSF already screened; the EU-overlap simply dedupes at the index. Keyless public API. Parser assumption: FSF-style semicolon CSV with WholeName columns — the first live run verifies; a wrong assumption parses 0 names and discloses DEGRADED, never a silent all-clear.

sources.name: Monaco — National Fund-Freezing List (Gel des fonds, JSON)
sources._note: Monaco's national freeze register (mirrors UN/EU/France plus Monaco's own 1373 designations by Ministerial Decision). Direct keyless JSON; the generic JSON parser assembles French name keys (nom/prenom/nomComplet) like the France DGT source. Added 2026-08-05; verify on the first live run.

sources.name: Latvia — FID National Sanctions List (XML)
sources._note: Latvia's small NATIONAL designation list (EU-FSF-style XML schema; generic XML extractor). Deliberately tiny floor — the list holds single-digit-to-dozens entries and a 0-name parse must still read as degraded, never as coverage.

sources.name: Israel — NBCTF Terror Designations (individuals, XLSX)
sources._note: Israel NBCTF terror-designation individuals (stable un-dated XLSX). RE-ENABLED 2026-08-05 on probe evidence: the runner fetches the real 87KB workbook (http 200) — the earlier 0-parse was the HEADER LAYOUT (Hebrew captions on row 0, English header 'Name of Individual - English/Hebrew/Arabic' on row 1), which the XLSX reader's header-row scan now handles; name columns carry all three scripts into the transliteration nets. browserHeaders on for WAF safety.

sources.name: Saudi Arabia — PCCT National Terrorism List (XLSX)
sources._note: Saudi PCCT national terrorism list (English XLSX). RE-ENABLED 2026-08-05 on probe evidence: the workbook keeps individuals/entities/vessels on SEPARATE TABS and sheet1 is vessels (the 7 sub-floor 'names' were ships) — the XLSX reader now walks every worksheet. Floor kept at 100 pending the first full-parse count; ratchet upward once observed.

sources.name: Qatar — NCTC Unified Sanction List (JSON)
sources._note: Qatar NCTC unified record. RE-ENABLED 2026-08-05 on probe evidence: the endpoint serves real JSON (864 designations, ~1.45MB) MISLABELED as text/html; keys are fullNameEn/fullNameAr (now known to the generic JSON walker — English + Arabic names both screen). Verified end-to-end with browser headers; the portal-state URL is the documented one and the probe re-verifies it on demand.

sources.name: Hong Kong SAR — CEDB Targeted Financial Sanctions (UN-relayed XML)
sources._note: Machine-readable, but Hong Kong's TFS lists relay UNSC designations the un-consolidated source already screens daily — enabling would add fetch risk for ~zero recall. Kept configured for the day HK publishes autonomous designations.

sources.name: Turkey — MASAK asset-freeze lists (Law 6415/7262)
sources._note: Turkey's national B/C/D category freezes (~1,600 beyond the UN mirror) publish as bot-protected HTML/attachment pages — no stable machine-readable endpoint (2026-08-05 survey). Curated path per the EOCN doctrine: populate a curated file from the official pages via the four-eyes SOP, or revisit if MASAK publishes a feed.

sources.name: Egypt — MLCU Domestic Terrorist Lists
sources._note: Egypt's domestic lists (~3,500-7,000 persons — the largest national list in the MENA survey) publish as Arabic-schema XLSX behind bot protection; no keyless machine-readable path verified (2026-08-05). Too large to hand-curate; revisit with a dedicated fetch/parse spike if a stable endpoint is confirmed from the runner.

sources.name: Jordan — AMLU National Sanctions List
sources._note: Jordan AMLU national list. Probe evidence 2026-08-05: the runner CAN reach it (http 200 — the earlier '403 from Actions' note did not reproduce) but publication is a server-rendered HTML page (121KB, ASP.NET), not a machine-readable feed. Stays curated/disabled until an export endpoint is found; re-probe via source-probe.yml.

sources.name: Argentina — RePET (Registro Público de Personas y Entidades vinculadas al terrorismo)
sources._note: Argentina's national terrorism register (personas file). parser CORRECTED 2026-08-05 from 'json' to 'unjson' on source-probe evidence (run 31030989375, entidades sibling): the feed is the UN-consolidated-list schema in JSON, NOT the Spanish nombre/apellido keys the note assumed — records carry ordered UN name parts (FIRST_NAME/SECOND_NAME/THIRD_NAME/FOURTH_NAME/NAME) plus INDIVIDUAL_ALIAS[].ALIAS_NAME. The generic 'json' walker matched only FIRST_NAME, so it indexed a bare first name per individual and dropped every alias (a silent recall+precision loss); 'unjson' concatenates the parts and captures the aliases, mirroring screen.py's parse_un.

sources.name: Brazil — BCB Disqualified Persons (QGI, enforcement — not financial sanctions)
sources._note: BCB disqualifications (OData JSON, keyless). RE-ENABLED 2026-08-05 on probe evidence: the payload is clean {value:[{Nome:...}]} and the walker parses it — the live 0-parse difference was the FETCH (plain screening UA vs the browser-shaped request the probe validated). browserHeaders on; enforcement tier as named.

sources.name: Brazil — BCB Prohibited Entities (QGP, enforcement — not financial sanctions)
sources._note: Sibling of br-bcb-qgi (same OData service). RE-ENABLED with it 2026-08-05; probe shows 2 live entries — `optional: true` keeps a small/empty parse a valid state, never degraded coverage.

sources.name: Brazil — TCU Debarred Companies (Licitantes Inidôneos)
sources._note: Federal Court of Accounts debarment list (Oracle ORDS JSON, keyless; explicit limit=10000 defeats the ORDS 25-row default page — an unnoticed pagination default would silently under-screen). Debarment tier like the World Bank feed. Added 2026-08-05; verify keys + pagination on the first live run.

sources.name: Brazil — TCU Disqualified Individuals (Inabilitados)
sources._note: Sibling of br-tcu-inidoneos: individuals disqualified from public office for corruption-adjacent findings — a PEP-adjacent integrity signal for Brazilian counterparties. Same ORDS shape + explicit limit. Added 2026-08-05; verify on the first live run.

sources.name: Mexico — SAT Art. 69-B EFOS list (tax-integrity signal, not sanctions)
sources._note: Mexico SAT Art. 69-B EFOS list. ENABLED 2026-08-05 on probe evidence: 4.5MB latin-1 CSV, header row after two preamble rows, 'Nombre del Contribuyente' column. The fetcher decodes latin-1 per-source (UTF-8 decode corrupted accented names) and parseSatCsv screens ONLY live statuses (Presunto/Definitivo — a rebutted or court-cleared taxpayer never flags). TIER: tax-integrity signal for Mexican counterparties, not a financial-sanctions designation — the list name says so.

sources.name: ADB — Published Debarment & Suspension Register (cross-debarments incl.)
sources._note: ADB published debarment register incl. the 2010 MDB Mutual-Enforcement cross-debarments (~1,533 firms/individuals; debarment/procurement-integrity tier). ENABLED 2026-08-05, read via the size/offset paginator. Live-tuned on two screen runs: run 31038800488 → egress-blocked (apim.adb.org added to the sanctions-screen allowlist, #412); run 31041253382 → HTTP 400 because size=250 exceeds the API's page-size limit (its own links.next uses size=10). So size is pinned to the API's accepted 10 and maxPages raised to 170 (≥153 pages of 10 covers 1,533); the offset advances by ACTUAL page length. Floored at minNames 500 — a short/failed fetch reports DEGRADED (loud), never a silent short list.

sources.name: MDB debarments — EBRD (POST-only API) / IDB (Socrata export unconfirmed) / AfDB (export route unconfirmed) / World Bank (key-walled)
sources._note: 2026-08-05 survey record: EBRD's ineligible-entities endpoint (www.ebrd.com/bin/ebrd_dxp/filterlistservlet) is a form-encoded POST — the single-GET fetcher cannot call it (a POST-capable source option is a small follow-up); IDB's Socrata export (mydata.iadb.org rows.csv) and AfDB's CSV export route are documented but their exact dataset paths were unverifiable from the sandbox — promote to live entries once confirmed from a runner; the World Bank's every machine-readable route requires an API key (re-confirmed — stays rejected under the keyless doctrine). ADB (enabled above) already carries the 2010 Mutual-Enforcement cross-debarments of the other MDBs, so the marginal gap while these stay stubs is the non-cross-debarred remainder.

sources.name: New Zealand — Police designated entities (HTML) / MFAT Russia Sanctions Register (WAF-challenged XLSX)
sources._note: 2026-08-05 survey: the Police UNSCR-1373 designations (~22 non-UN entries) publish as HTML tables with periodic dated attachments (curated path); MFAT's Russia Sanctions Register XLSX has a stable keyless URL but sits behind an Imperva JS challenge that a plain fetch cannot pass — test from a runner before promoting; if the challenge holds, it stays curated. Supersedes the older nz-terror stub above.

sources.name: South Africa — FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions List (XML)
sources._note: South Africa FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions list. DISABLED 2026-08-05 on probe evidence: the configured URL (?fileType=xml on /Pages/TFSListDownload) returns an HTML LANDING PAGE ('TFS list downloads'), not the XML file — the real download-handler URL must be read off that page (a browser/curated step; the runner can reach the host, so this is a URL-discovery task, not a reachability block). Re-probe candidate once the direct file URL is captured.

sources.name: Africa national lists — Nigeria NigSAC / Kenya FRC / Mauritius NSSEC / Morocco CNASNU / Tunisia CNLCT / Ghana FIC
sources._note: 2026-08-05 survey record: Nigeria's domestic list (~31-50 entries) is HTML-only with per-entry detail pages; Kenya publishes dated XLSX filenames behind a landing page; Mauritius and Morocco publish PDFs/HTML; Tunisia is an HTML table on a plain-http origin; Ghana has no consolidated domestic list at all. All await official feeds or curated files via the four-eyes SOP. One documented stub, enabled:false — survey record, never counted as coverage.

sources.name: CIS national lists — Kazakhstan AFM (gated 2025) / Kyrgyzstan FIU (rotating filenames) / Azerbaijan FMS (link-discovery) / Georgia (gazette HTML) / Armenia (dated PDFs) / Moldova (UN-duplicate)
sources._note: 2026-08-05 survey record: Kazakhstan's Web-SFM endpoint became key-gated ~Sep 2025 (rejected under the keyless doctrine); Kyrgyzstan's FIU XML rotates its filename each update and Azerbaijan's FMS XML sits behind an index page — both need HTML link-discovery the single-GET fetcher deliberately does not do (a future fetch feature, not a source entry); Georgia's Otkhozoria-Tatunashvili list (~33 names) and Armenia's national designations publish as gazette HTML / dated PDFs (curated path); Moldova's CAS-SIS list consolidates UN lists already screened. One documented stub, enabled:false — survey record, never counted as coverage.

sources.name: Asia national lists — Japan MOF / Korea KoFIU / Taiwan MOJ / Singapore TSOFA / Indonesia DTTOT / Malaysia MOHA / Philippines AMLC / Thailand AMLO / India MHA / Pakistan NACTA / Bahrain / Oman / Kuwait
sources._note: 2026-08-05 worldwide survey verdict: these national lists publish only as HTML pages, PDFs, or dated-filename spreadsheets — no stable keyless machine-readable endpoint (details in the survey record; Japan MOF uses dated XLSX names, Singapore's TSOFA First Schedule is statute HTML, Indonesia's DTTOT is a page of dated attachments, Pakistan NACTA is HTML tables). Their UN-relayed content is already screened via un-consolidated; the national increments await either official feeds or curated files via the four-eyes SOP. One documented stub instead of thirteen: this entry is the survey's record, not screening coverage — enabled:false means it never counts as screened.
